body_en: The US president oscillates between strike threats on Iran and insisting the war ‘militarily is effectively over’

A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post on Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.

The Roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September. It joins the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as smaller navy ships, which are in the region to maintain a naval blockade of Iranian shipping.

The George HW Bush arrived in the region in April, while the George Washington arrived in August. The navy previously had three carrier strike groups in the Middle East in April, for the first time since 2003.

In addition to the three aircraft carriers, the flotilla in the Arabian Sea now includes 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship, according to the navy. Two more destroyers are in the Red Sea.

The Roosevelt had deployed along with the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group, which includes the USS John P Murtha and USS Anchorage amphibious landing ships and around 2,000 marines. Those ships have yet to make it to the region.

The third carrier arrived nearly two weeks after midterm elections that saw voters deliver major losses to Trump’s Republican party, driven in part by the unpopularity of the Iran war and its economic effects. The results led JD Vance to publicly break with Trump over the conflict, posting on social media that “the reason we lost is the war”.
Trump has insisted it was the right thing to do and has not ruled out restarting the conflict, which has been locked in a stalemate for months.
Last week, Trump warned Iran that the US military is “locked and loaded” and that the US was keeping an eye on Pickaxe Mountain, a facility linked to Iran’s nuclear program, for signs of activity.
“If something does not work out, I would not hesitate” to act, Trump told conservative broadcaster Hugh Hewitt on Thursday.

Yet, Trump also told reporters last week that he believed it was highly unlikely he would need to order new major strikes on Iran, declaring that the war “militarily is effectively over” after meeting with Qatar’s prime minister.

Trump also declared that the US no longer needs a deal with Tehran and told Vance – who was a chief negotiator in earlier ceasefire talks – instead to focus on the administration’s domestic anti-fraud campaign targeting Democratic-controlled cities and states.

Negotiations have stalled due to differences over Iran’s nuclear program, an issue that Trump insists be part of any deal meant to end the war. Iran wants the US first to agree to several core conditions, including lifting the naval blockade that is stopping its oil from getting to world markets.
In the meantime, a focal point of the simmering conflict remains the strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway where a fifth of the world’s oil passed before the war.

Commercial ships are still coming under attack or facing other risks, while the US has carried out limited strikes on Iranian targets near the strait and is helping guide vessels through the contested waters.
Iranian state TV, quoting the naval arm of Iran’s revolutionary guard and the army, warned shipping companies Monday that a US-supported route through the waterway is dangerous because of mines.
Mines have damaged six oil tankers since Sunday, polluting the strait’s coastlines, according to the revolutionary guard’s navy.
Separately, a projectile struck a tanker trying to transit through the strait, starting an engine room fire, but no casualties were reported, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Organization said.
body_zh: 美国总统在对伊朗进行打击威胁和坚称战争“军事上实际上已经结束”之间摇摆不定
美国中央司令部周一在社交媒体帖子中表示，美国第三艘航空母舰已抵达中东，这戏剧性地展示了军事实力，而唐纳德·特朗普则为伊朗战争的下一步行动保留了选择余地。
西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰向中东增派了数千名士兵，特朗普在威胁对伊朗进行进一步大规模打击和坚称这场持续八个多月的战争“在军事上实际上已经结束”之间摇摆不定。
罗斯福号及其随行打击部队于九月离开圣地亚哥。它与乔治·H·W·布什号航空母舰和乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰以及小型海军舰艇一起在该地区维持对伊朗航运的海上封锁。
乔治·H·W·布什号于四月抵达该地区，而乔治·华盛顿号则于八月抵达该地区。此前，海军于4月份在中东部署了三个航母战斗群，这是自2003年以来的首次。
据海军称，除了三艘航空母舰外，阿​​拉伯海的舰队目前还包括 13 艘驱逐舰、两艘巡洋舰和一艘濒海战斗舰。还有两艘驱逐舰正在红海。
罗斯福号与马金岛号两栖战备大队一起部署，该大队包括约翰·P·穆萨号和安克雷奇号两栖登陆舰以及大约 2,000 名海军陆战队员。这些船只尚未抵达该地区。
第三艘航母在中期选举近两周后抵达，选民们给特朗普领导的共和党带来了重大损失，部分原因是伊朗战争不受欢迎及其经济影响。结果导致JD万斯在冲突问题上公开与特朗普决裂，并在社交媒体上发帖称“我们失败的原因是战争”。
特朗普坚称这是正确的做法，并且不排除重新启动冲突的可能性，冲突已陷入僵局数月。
上周，特朗普警告伊朗，美军已“上膛并上膛”，并且美国正在密切关注与伊朗核计划有关的镐山设施，寻找活动迹象。
特朗普周四对保守派广播公司休·休伊特表示，“如果事情没有解决，我会毫不犹豫地”采取行动。
然而，特朗普上周还告诉记者，他认为他不太可能下令对伊朗进行新的大规模打击，并在与卡塔尔总理会面后宣布战争“在军事上实际上已经结束”。
特朗普还宣布美国不再需要与德黑兰达成协议，并告诉万斯 — — 他是早期停火谈判的首席谈判代表 — — 而是将重点放在政府针对民主党控制的城市和州的国内反欺诈运动上。
由于对伊朗核计划的分歧，谈判陷入僵局，特朗普坚称这一问题是任何旨在结束战争的协议的一部分。伊朗希望美国首先同意几个核心条件，包括解除阻止其石油进入世界市场的海上封锁。
与此同时，日益激烈的冲突的焦点仍然是霍尔木兹海峡，这是一条重要的水道，战前世界上五分之一的石油都经过这里。
商船仍然受到攻击或面临其他风险，而美国对海峡附近的伊朗目标进行了有限的打击，并正在帮助引导船只通过有争议的水域。
伊朗国家电视台周一援引伊朗革命卫队海军部队和陆军的消息警告航运公司，美国支持的这条水道航线因地雷而存在危险。
据革命卫队海军称，自周日以来，地雷已损坏了六艘油轮，污染了海峡的海岸线。
英国海事贸易组织表示，另外一枚炮弹击中了一艘试图通过该海峡的油轮，引发机舱火灾，但没有人员伤亡报告。

title_en: Read the full White House memo requiring agencies to get approval before testifying in front of Congress
title_zh: 阅读完整的白宫备忘录，要求各机构在国会面前作证之前获得批准
summary: In a new memorandum obtained by PBS News on Monday, White House counsel Will Scharf is directing all federal agencies and executive departments to get approval from White House legal and legislative affairs offices before agreeing to testify before congression
summary_zh: 在 PBS 新闻周一获得的一份新备忘录中，白宫法律顾问威尔·沙夫指示所有联邦机构和行政部门
body_en: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/read-the-full-white-house-memo-requiring-agencies-to-get-approval-before-testifying-in-front-of-congress

In a new memorandum obtained by PBS News on Monday, White House counsel Will Scharf is directing all federal agencies and executive departments to get approval from White House legal and legislative affairs offices before agreeing to testify before congressional committees.
Read the full memo by clicking the image below.
The directive comes as both chambers of Congress prepare for incoming Democratic leadership, which has promised robust oversight of the Trump administration after sweeping victories in the midterms.

A White House official told PBS News in an emailed statement: "The Trump Administration will not be extorted, intimidated, or threatened into submission by politically motivated baseless investigations. We are ready to engage with Congress, this process ensures reasonable requests are respected, but baseless political attempts to undermine our mission will not be accepted as the status quo by Democrats' who want to slow the administration down from its historic work."
Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Agencies can fulfill "legitimate congressional oversight requests while keeping Cabinet officials focused on their foremost responsibility: serving the American people and delivering results for them," the official wrote.

The latest directive from Scharf follows a separate letter he sent last week to Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, claiming that pledges by Democrats to investigate Trump and his administration "may cross the line into blatant criminality." That three-page letter accused Democrats of "abusive and capricious threats" against Trump and administration officials.
WATCH: Rep. Garcia says voters gave Democrats a mandate to pursue accountability

The White House official pointed to four letters that House Democrats have sent to federal agencies like the Department of Homeland Security asking for documents to be preserved, referring to them as "exorbitant demands Democrats have sent the agencies."

The Trump administration, in particular the Department of Justice, has investigated and in some cases prosecuted some of the president's perceived political enemies like former FBI Director James Comey during his second term.
A free press is a cornerstone of a healthy democracy.
Support trusted journalism and civil dialogue.

Liz Landers is a correspondent for PBS News Hour, where she covers the White House and the Trump administration. Prior to joining the News Hour, she served as the national security correspondent for Scripps News, and also reported on disinformation for the network.
body_zh: 在美国公共广播公司新闻周一获得的一份新备忘录中，白宫法律顾问威尔·沙夫指示所有联邦机构和行政部门在同意在国会委员会作证之前获得白宫法律和立法事务办公室的批准。
单击下图阅读完整的备忘录。
该指令出台之际，国会参众两院正在为即将上任的民主党领导层做准备，民主党承诺在中期选举中大获全胜后对特朗普政府进行强有力的监督。
一名白宫官员在一份电子邮件声明中告诉美国公共广播公司新闻：“特朗普政府不会因出于政治动机的毫无根据的调查而被勒索、恐吓或威胁屈服。我们已准备好与国会接触，这一程序确保合理的要求得到尊重，但破坏我们使命的毫无根据的政治企图不会被民主党人接受，因为他们希望减缓政府的历史性工作。”
与自由和独立的新闻业站在一起。加入 PBS 新闻的记者通行证
这位官员写道，各机构可以满足“国会的合法监督要求，同时让内阁官员专注于他们的首要责任：为美国人民服务并为他们带来成果”。
沙夫在发出最新指令之前，他上周向众议院监督委员会民主党籍众议员罗伯特·加西亚（D-Calif.）发送了一封单独的信，声称民主党调查特朗普及其政府的承诺“可能会跨越公然犯罪的界限”。这封长达三页的信指责民主党对特朗普和政府官员进行“辱骂和反复无常的威胁”。
观看：众议员加西亚表示选民授权民主党追究责任
这位白宫官员指出，众议院民主党人已向国土安全部等联邦机构发出四封信，要求保留文件，称这些信件是“民主党人向这些机构提出的过高要求”。
特朗普政府，特别是司法部，在他的第二个任期内调查并在某些情况下起诉了总统的一些被视为政敌，例如前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米。
新闻自由是健康民主的基石。
支持值得信赖的新闻报道和民间对话。
莉兹·兰德斯 (Liz Landers) 是 PBS News Hour 的记者，报道白宫和特朗普政府的情况。在加入“新闻一小时”之前，她曾担任斯克里普斯新闻的国家安全记者，并为该网络报道虚假信息。

title_en: Suspect in custody after bomb found at Illinois ethanol plant
title_zh: 伊利诺伊州乙醇工厂发现炸弹后嫌疑人被拘留
summary: The FBI is leading the investigation into the Biourja Renewables incident after it led to a temporary evacuation Authorities investigating a bomb found recently at an ethanol production plant in Peoria, Illinois, have taken a suspect into custody, according to
summary_zh: 比乌尔哈可再生能源公司事件导致临时疏散，联邦调查局正在牵头调查当局正在调查炸弹发现事件
body_en: The FBI is leading the investigation into the Biourja Renewables incident after it led to a temporary evacuation
Authorities investigating a bomb found recently at an ethanol production plant in Peoria, Illinois, have taken a suspect into custody, according to the mayor there.
The Peoria mayor, Rita Ali, told the Guardian on Monday that leadership at the BioUrja Renewables plant “have informed me that a suspect is in custody”.
Ali said the FBI – which is leading the investigation into the bomb – is expected to release more details later.

In a separate statement on Monday, the FBI’s division in nearby Springfield, Illinois, announced that its agents “were conducting law enforcement activity … in connection with the Biourja Renewables explosives device incident”.

“The investigation remains ongoing,” said the FBI, which added that it was receiving assistance from the federal bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Illinois state police, the local sheriff’s office, the Peoria police department and the police department of adjacent East Peoria.
The Guardian has contacted the FBI for additional comment.

Ali’s comments came after her administration ordered thousands of residents in parts of Peoria to evacuate their homes and businesses because authorities discovered an explosive device at BioUrja Renewables.
The ethanol for fuel and alcohol which the plant produces is highly flammable. And the riverfront facility spans an area that is roughly equivalent to 44.5 US football fields.
The Peoria police chief, Brad Dixon, said a potential explosion could have affected an area within a one-mile radius – but that technicians had rendered the bomb safe.

The evacuation zone ordered by local authorities encompassed a part of East Peoria, which is a separate municipality. Local events were canceled as streets in the affected area were closed to the public.

Officials lifted the evacuation order at about 1.25pm on Saturday after they determined that no additional explosives had been found. They didn’t immediately announce any arrests but made clear they were working to identify any suspects in connection with the bomb.

Bomb threats and suspicious package calls are relatively common for law enforcement. Officials take those kinds of calls seriously as they investigate them. But they often aren’t verified as credible or substantial, making the case in Peoria – a city with about 110,000 residents – somewhat rare.
body_zh: 比乌尔哈可再生能源公司事件导致临时疏散，联邦调查局正在牵头调查
据伊利诺伊州皮奥里亚市市长称，当局正在调查最近在伊利诺伊州皮奥里亚一家乙醇生产厂发现的一枚炸弹，并已拘留一名嫌疑人。
皮奥里亚市市长丽塔·阿里 (Rita Ali) 周一告诉《卫报》，BioUrja 可再生能源工厂的领导层“已通知我，一名嫌疑人已被拘留”。
阿里表示，领导炸弹调查的联邦调查局预计稍后会公布更多细节。
在周一的另一份声明中，联邦调查局位于伊利诺伊州斯普林菲尔德附近的部门宣布，其特工“正在针对比乌尔贾可再生能源爆炸装置事件……开展执法活动”。
FBI 表示：“调查仍在进行中。”该机构补充说，它正在接受联邦烟酒枪械和爆炸物局 (ATF)、伊利诺伊州警察局、当地治安官办公室、皮奥里亚警察局以及邻近的东皮奥里亚警察局的协助。
《卫报》已联系联邦调查局寻求更多评论。
阿里发表此番言论之前，她的政府下令皮奥里亚部分地区的数千名居民撤离家园和企业，因为当局在 BioUrja 可再生能源公司发现了爆炸装置。
该工厂生产的燃料乙醇和酒精高度易燃。河滨设施的面积大约相当于 44.5 个美国足球场。
皮奥里亚警察局长布拉德·迪克森表示，潜在的爆炸可能会影响半径一英里内的区域，但技术人员已确保炸弹安全。
地方当局下令的疏散区包括东皮奥里亚的一部分，该市是一个独立的自治市。由于受影响地区的街道对公众关闭，当地活动被取消。
周六下午 1 点 25 分左右，官员们确定没有发现更多爆炸物后取消了疏散令。他们没有立即宣布逮捕任何人，但明确表示他们正在努力查明与炸弹有关的任何嫌疑人。
炸弹威胁和可疑包裹电话对于执法部门来说相对常见。官员们在调查过程中认真对待此类电话。但它们往往没有被证实为可信或实质性的，这使得皮奥里亚这个拥有约 11 万居民的城市的案例有些罕见。

title_en: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
title_zh: 由于英伟达的影响，美国加强了对远程访问人工智能技术的控制
summary: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.
summary_zh: 新规则弥补了一个存在的漏洞，该漏洞允许中国公司仍然远程访问先进的人工智能芯片，尽管美国对此有限制。
body_en: Data center company Megaspeed International's office in Singapore on Nov. 10, 2026. The company is suspected of selling remote access to U.S. AI chips to Chinese companies. A new Commerce Department rule would restrict that access. Taryn Ng/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

The U.S. government has announced a rule to prevent remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers, closing a loophole that could let adversarial governments access American AI technology through overseas data centers.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal

The move comes amid the fallout at Nvidia, the world's dominant producer of AI chips, following revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence officials suspected of being a Chinese intelligence operative. NPR has not independently verified the claims. Huang stepped down as CEO last week.

Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, is a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company. Jensen Huang has personally lobbied President Trump to loosen restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to China. It is not known if Alice Huang influenced this activity.
Trump administration backs off Nvidia H20 chip crackdown after Mar-a-Lago dinner

The rapid advancement in cloud computing and AI infrastructure has made it possible to access advanced U.S. computing capabilities remotely, including through data centers located outside countries subject to U.S. export restrictions, the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) said in a statement on Monday.

The rule is designed to reinforce existing restrictions on access to sensitive American AI technology through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in other countries, which could threaten national security
However, a loophole existed where Chinese companies could still access those chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

"The United States is the global leader in advanced computing and super intelligence technology and is committed to promoting the global adoption of American technology for legitimate commercial purposes while ensuring that sensitive technologies are not exploited in ways that threaten U.S. national security," the BIS statement said.
The government refers to artificial intelligence as "super intelligence" following an executive order signed by President Trump in September.

Since October 2022, U.S. companies have typically needed a BIS export license to sell advanced computing chips meeting specified technical thresholds to China, including Hong Kong and Macau. These restrictions covered advanced Nvidia chips, some high-performance semiconductor components, and certain AI computing systems.
Megaspeed is based in Singapore and operates facilities in Malaysia.

"Megaspeed conducts legitimate and lawful business. The company has retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation," the company said in a statement emailed to NPR and other news organizations on Sunday.
Prior to the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration had resisted imposing additional regulations to prevent foreign access to American AI technology.

The Biden administration had written a framework designed to control worldwide distribution of advanced AI chips on January 15, 2025 – five days before Trump's inauguration. In May 2025, Trump's Commerce Department announced it would not enforce the rule and intended to rescind it, calling it "ill-conceived and counterproductive."

Biden's framework would have also limited access to AI chips by countries considered security risks, required licenses for certain chip exports, and created restrictions on the power of advanced models and computing infrastructure.

The New York Times reported that Trump was first briefed by intelligence officials about Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy in October 2025. Both Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are expected to testify before Congress this month and next month and there will likely be further investigations into what Trump knew about the affair when the Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027, Rep. Yvette Clarke, D-NY, told NPR.

"We need to get the facts investigated, bring in individuals to give us as much information as possible under oath, so that we can get to the bottom of why this happened, how it occurred, and how we could prevent this type of compromise from happening again," said Clarke.
body_zh: 2026 年 11 月 10 日，数据中心公司 Megaspeed International 位于新加坡的办公室。该公司涉嫌向中国公司出售对美国人工智能芯片的远程访问。商务部的一项新规则将限制这种访问。 Taryn Ng/法新社，来自盖蒂图片社 隐藏标题栏
美国政府宣布了一项规则，禁止远程访问先进的人工智能芯片和服务器，堵住敌对政府通过海外数据中心访问美国人工智能技术的漏洞。
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌间谍丑闻辞职
此举正值全球主要人工智能芯片生产商英伟达受到影响之际，此前英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名被美国情报官员怀疑为中国情报人员的女性发生了恋情。 NPR 尚未独立核实这些说法。黄上周辞去首席执行官职务。
与 Jensen Huang 无亲属关系的 Alice Huang 是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed International 的前高管。黄仁勋亲自游说特朗普总统放宽对英伟达芯片向中国销售的限制。目前尚不清楚 Alice Huang 是否影响了这项活动。
海湖庄园晚宴后，特朗普政府放弃了对 Nvidia H20 芯片的打击
美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）周一在一份声明中表示，云计算和人工智能基础设施的快速发展使得远程访问美国先进的计算能力成为可能，包括通过位于受美国出口限制的国家之外的数据中心。
该规则旨在加强对通过涉及其他国家数据中心的远程计算安排获取美国敏感人工智能技术的现有限制，这可能威胁国家安全
然而，存在一个漏洞，尽管美国限制向中国出售这些芯片，但中国公司仍然可以远程访问这些芯片。
BIS 声明称：“美国是先进计算和超级智能技术的全球领导者，致力于促进全球采用美国技术用于合法商业目的，同时确保敏感技术不被以威胁美国国家安全的方式利用。”
特朗普总统于 9 月签署行政命令后，政府将人工智能称为“超级智能”。
自 2022 年 10 月以来，美国公司通常需要获得 BIS 出口许可证才能向中国（包括香港和澳门）销售符合特定技术门槛的先进计算芯片。这些限制涵盖先进的 Nvidia 芯片、一些高性能半导体组件以及某些人工智能计算系统。
Megaspeed 总部位于新加坡，在马来西亚设有工厂。
“Megaspeed 开展合法、合法的业务。该公司已聘请外部法律顾问来进行彻底的内部调查，”该公司在周日通过电子邮件发送给 NPR 和其他新闻机构的声明中表示。
在英伟达丑闻发生之前，特朗普政府一直拒绝实施额外的法规来阻止外国企业获取美国人工智能技术。
拜登政府于 2025 年 1 月 15 日（即特朗普就职前五天）编写了一个旨在控制先进人工智能芯片在全球范围内分发的框架。 2025 年 5 月，特朗普的商务部宣布不会执行该规则，并打算废除该规则，称其“考虑不周且适得其反”。
拜登的框架还将限制被视为安全风险的国家获得人工智能芯片，某些芯片出口需要许可证，并对先进模型和计算基础设施的能力设置限制。
据《纽约时报》报道，情报官员于 2025 年 10 月首次向特朗普通报了黄仁勋与一名疑似中国间谍的恋情。纽约州民主党众议员伊薇特·克拉克 (Yvette Clarke) 告诉 NPR，黄仁勋和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克预计将于本月和下个月在国会作证，当民主党于 2027 年 1 月控制国会时，可能会进一步调查特朗普对该事件的了解情况。
克拉克说：“我们需要调查事实，让个人在宣誓后向我们提供尽可能多的信息，以便我们能够查清此事发生的原因、如何发生以及我们如何防止此类妥协再次发生。”

title_en: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
title_zh: 随着对人工智能武器的担忧加剧，联合国会谈寻求遏制“杀手机器人”
summary: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.
summary_zh: 各国正在日内瓦举行会议，就无需人为干预即可选择和杀死目标的武器规则进行谈判。但与美国、俄罗斯
body_en: An armed robot developed by Turkish defense companies is demonstrated at a facility in Duzce, Turkey, on April 29. Omer Urer/Anadolu via Getty Images hide caption
GENEVA — Negotiations on possible rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, also known as 'killer robots' are underway at the United Nations in Geneva.

Supporters of controls on autonomous weapons say this week's U.N. conference on Certain Conventional Weapons (or CCW), which meets just once every five years, is the last best chance to agree rules before it is too late.

Warfare technology has advanced rapidly in the last few years, with some experts warning that the world is just months away from having weapons that can choose targets and make the decision to kill autonomously.
AI and autonomous weapons are high on the agenda at the UN General Assembly

In Ukraine and Gaza, AI-assisted weapons have already been used to take out targets, with Ukrainian civilians reporting being 'hunted' by drones as they shop or go to school. But these are still controlled remotely by humans.

Humanitarian organizations say the decision to kill – and responsibility for that choice – must stay in human hands. Ahead of this week's meeting, the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Pope have all called for legally binding rules. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that allowing fully autonomous weapons to kill would be 'crossing a moral red line'.

The Red Cross is especially worried that existing rules of war – the Geneva Conventions – cannot be fully respected by autonomous weapons. War is often chaotic and confusing, and the situation can change rapidly. Under the Conventions, soldiers who are wounded or in the process of surrendering can no longer be targeted.
How drones are reshaping modern warfare around the globe

Georgia Haines, a legal adviser with the Red Cross, worries that autonomous weapons will not be able to distinguish between a soldier who is still fighting, one who is wounded and one who wants to surrender.

'The risk is that, based on the technology we are seeing, they are not able to understand in the same way that a human is the contextual signals. And so the risks are incredibly high that there will be a misidentification of a target.'

Meanwhile, human rights groups warn that the technology behind AI-assisted weapons is becoming increasingly cheap and easy to use. The more it is adopted by the military, the greater the danger of proliferation and its use by terrorist groups or law enforcement agencies in repressive regimes. In theory , a swarm of autonomous drones could be programmed to kill everyone wearing a red sweater, everyone carrying a poster or even everyone speaking a certain language.

Many of the countries now meeting in Geneva take such concerns very seriously. At least 50, including Ireland, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, France and Germany, are calling for a strict timetable to agree on binding rules governing autonomous weapons.

But among states that are already developing and using semi-autonomous weapons, there is pushback. The United States, Russia and Israel have indicated they are set to oppose legally binding rules, with Washington proposing a five-year timetable to draft non-binding guidelines instead.
How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war

The U.S. is traditionally a late adopter of international treaties. It did not ratify the Ottawa Convention on landmines, for example, although it did, over time, stop deploying them and reduce its stockpiles.

Under President Trump, doubts about international law have grown. Washington has imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court, and just this weekend, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in a keynote speech to the Federalist Society, warned against "quoting laws to men with swords."

The problem for states meeting in Geneva is that U.N. negotiations on limiting specific weapons are supposed to be conducted by consensus. This was achieved in 1995, when countries agreed to a ban on blinding lasers, but other agreements have proved elusive. With landmines, countries frustrated by the delay finally took negotiations outside the U.N. process to create the Ottawa Convention.

This week, there may be a compromise: a longer or even open-ended negotiating period to come up with rules that individual states can adopt as binding or non-binding. For diplomats supporting such a solution, it is a way to ensure at least some progress. For campaigners, it is less than ideal, with one likening it to kicking a very dangerous can down the road.
body_zh: 4 月 29 日，土耳其国防公司开发的武装机器人在土耳其迪兹杰的一处设施中进行展示。Omer Urer/Anadolu via Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
日内瓦——位于日内瓦的联合国正在就使用致命自主武器（也称为“杀手机器人”）的可能规则进行谈判。
自主武器管制的支持者表示，本周召开的联合国特定常规武器会议每五年举行一次，是在为时已晚之前达成规则的最后最佳机会。
战争技术在过去几年中迅速发展，一些专家警告说，世界距离拥有能够选择目标并自主做出杀伤决定的武器只有几个月的时间。
人工智能和自主武器是联合国大会议程的重要议题
在乌克兰和加沙，人工智能辅助武器已经被用来消灭目标，乌克兰平民报告说，他们在购物或上学时遭到无人机“追捕”。但这些仍然是由人类远程控制的。
人道主义组织表示，杀戮的决定以及这一选择的责任必须掌握在人类手中。在本周的会议之前，联合国、红十字国际委员会和教皇都呼吁制定具有法律约束力的规则。联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯警告说，允许完全自主的武器杀人将“跨越道德红线”。
红十字会尤其担心自主武器无法充分遵守现有的战争规则——《日内瓦公约》。战争往往是混乱无序、局势瞬息万变的。根据公约，受伤或正在投降的士兵不能再成为攻击目标。
无人机如何重塑全球现代战争
红十字会法律顾问乔治亚·海恩斯担心，自主武器将无法区分仍在战斗的​​士兵、受伤的士兵和想要投降的士兵。
“风险在于，根据我们所看到的技术，它们无法像人类那样理解上下文信号。因此，错误识别目标的风险非常高。”
与此同时，人权组织警告说，人工智能辅助武器背后的技术正变得越来越便宜且易于使用。军队采用的越多，扩散以及被恐怖组织或专制政权的执法机构使用的危险就越大。理论上，一群自主无人机可以被编程杀死每个穿红色毛衣的人、每个携带海报的人，甚至每个人说某种语言的人。
目前在日内瓦召开会议的许多国家都非常重视此类关切。包括爱尔兰、意大利、巴西、墨西哥、法国和德国在内的至少 50 个国家呼吁制定严格的时间表，以就管理自主武器的约束性规则达成一致。
但在已经开发和使用半自主武器的国家中，却出现了阻力。美国、俄罗斯和以色列已表示他们将反对具有法律约束力的规则，而华盛顿则提出了一个五年时间表来起草不具约束力的指导方针。
人工智能无人机如何影响乌克兰战争的进程
传统上，美国是国际条约的较晚采用者。例如，它没有批准关于地雷的《渥太华公约》，尽管随着时间的推移，它确实停止部署地雷并减少库存。
在特朗普总统的领导下，人们对国际法的怀疑有所增加。华盛顿对国际刑事法院实施了全面制裁，就在本周末，国务卿马可·卢比奥在联邦党人协会的主题演讲中警告不要“向持剑之人引用法律”。
各国在日内瓦举行会议的问题是，联合国关于限制特定武器的谈判应该以协商一致方式进行。这一目标于 1995 年实现，当时各国同意禁止致盲激光，但事实证明其他协议难以达成。由于地雷问题，因拖延而感到沮丧的国家最终在联合国制定《渥太华公约》的进程之外进行了谈判。
本周，可能会达成妥协：更长甚至不限成员名额的谈判期，以制定各国可以采用的有约束力或无约束力的规则。对于支持这种解决方案的外交官来说，这是确保至少取得一些进展的一种方式。对于活动人士来说，这并不理想，有人将其比作将一个非常危险的罐子踢到路上。

title_en: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
title_zh: 美国有近 200 万人入狱。我们是怎么到这里的？

This is FRESH AIR. I'm Dave Davies. You might remember the controversy surrounding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's plan to livestream the execution of the man convicted of a mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas. The livestreaming plan was called off, but in colonial times, executions of criminals were among the largest public gatherings. Eight thousand people converged on Boston in 1773 to witness the hanging of Levi Ames, convicted of multiple acts of burglary. That story is among the revelations in a remarkable documentary series about crime and punishment in America coming to PBS this week, directed by our guest today, Lynn Novick.

The four-part series takes us from a day when prisons were largely unknown to the America of today, where nearly 2 million people are behind bars, a rate far higher than other industrialized countries. There are stories of criminal defendants, both innocent and guilty, as well as victims, police, prosecutors, judges and countless politicians who staked their fortunes on fighting crime. It raises critical questions and explores multiple points of view about how to answer them.

Lynn Novick is an award-winning documentary filmmaker who's collaborated with Ken Burns on many of his acclaimed series. Her most recent series, "College Behind Bars," was about men and women earning college degrees while incarcerated. Her series "Crime And Punishment In America" will air over four consecutive nights on PBS beginning tonight.
LYNN NOVICK: Thank you so much for having me, Dave. It's a pleasure to be here.

DAVIES: You know, you could do a long documentary series on crime in post-war America, or crime since the '90s, or crime in urban areas, or - I mean, in this case, you really take on a lot, going back to the beginning of the Republic. How did you come to decide to take on such a sprawling subject?

NOVICK: Yeah, it is a sprawling subject. For me, it felt like an opportunity to revisit the last 250 years of American history, which we have explored in other projects I've worked on with Ken Burns - history of jazz, history of baseball most notably - where we take a topic, an idea, and we look at all of American history through that lens. And it felt like no one had done this before, and the way that we address crime and the way that we punish and how we - why we have prisons and why we incarcerate at the rate that we do, all of these things didn't just come out of nowhere. And I wanted to understand how we got here, and the only way to do that was to kind of go back to the beginning and follow the breadcrumbs, so to speak, wherever they would lead.

DAVIES: You know, going back to colonial times, punishment for crimes was typically physical and quite public. How likely back then would an ordinary citizen be to witness an execution sometime in his or her life?

NOVICK: Yeah. I was stunned to learn from a number of our scholars and experts that executions were common in colonial America for a whole range of crimes. Not just what we would think of today of very serious, violent crimes - murder, rape, etc. - but you could be put to death for burglary, adultery, blasphemy, you know, robbery - just a wide range of crimes. And from what we understand, most people in colonial America would have seen an execution at some point in their lifetime. That is staggering to me.
DAVIES: Was - I mean, was this because they - it was believed that this would deter crime, or was there simply just such an interest in these public executions?

NOVICK: I think the answer is both, truly - that we've always been fascinated by those who transgress, who don't follow the rules and who get caught and have to pay the price. So that's - and that's not just Americans. Human beings are (ph) always been interested in, you know, who are the outlaws, the criminals, and, you know, why did they do the thing they did? And we want to see them punished.

And why punishment was administered publicly was, I believe, partly to deter - that was the idea - to shame, to just sort of send a message to everyone about the power of the state. So there's - it's serving a - to sort of knit together the social structure, you know, to build community, I suppose - that this is what we as a community do to those who, you know, disobey our rules. But as it turns out, it could have a sort of undermining effect of all those things as well. A huge crowd could gather at an execution and they might sort of start rabble-rousing, and you might even have a riot, and people might get hurt or robbed in the process of getting sort of excited about the execution. They might identify with the person who was being put to death and feel that it was unjust.

And so by the time of the revolution, some of our Founding Fathers who were really studying the enlightenment and thinking about what do citizens deserve in a republic and what kind of rights we should have began to put forth the idea that this public punishment and the sort of barbaric nature of it was actually bad for the society as a whole and that we should come up with a better way of doing this.
DAVIES: Right. Well, one alternative to physical punishment is confinement, and that leads us to prisons. What were early prisons like?

这是新鲜空气。我是戴夫·戴维斯。您可能还记得围绕国防部长皮特·赫格斯计划直播德克萨斯州胡德堡大规模枪击案男子的处决而引发的争议。直播计划被取消，但在殖民时期，处决罪犯是最大规模的公众集会之一。 1773 年，八千人聚集在波士顿，目睹了因多项入室盗窃罪被判绞刑的利维·艾姆斯 (Levi Ames)。这个故事是本周由我们今天的嘉宾林恩·诺维克 (Lynn Novick) 执导的 PBS 一部关于美国犯罪与惩罚的精彩纪录片系列中的揭露内容之一。
这部由四部分组成的系列剧带我们回顾了当今美国对监狱几乎一无所知的一天，那里有近 200 万人被关在监狱里，这一比例远远高于其他工业化国家。其中有无辜和有罪的刑事被告、受害者、警察、检察官、法官和无数将自己的财富押在打击犯罪上的政客的故事。它提出了关键问题，并探讨了如何回答这些问题的多种观点。
林恩·诺维克 (Lynn Novick) 是一位屡获殊荣的纪录片制片人，他与肯·伯恩斯 (Ken Burns) 合作拍摄了许多广受好评的剧集。她最近的系列剧《监狱里的大学》讲述了男人和女人在监禁期间获得大学学位的故事。她的连续剧《美国的罪与罚》将从今晚开始在 PBS 连续四晚播出。
林恩·诺维克：戴夫，非常感谢您邀请我。很高兴来到这里。
戴维斯：你知道，你可以制作一部关于战后美国犯罪的长纪录片系列，或者自 90 年代以来的犯罪，或者城市地区的犯罪，或者 - 我的意思是，在这种情况下，你真的承担了很多，可以追溯到共和国之初。您是如何决定研究这样一个庞大的主题的？

诺维克：是的，这是一个庞大的主题。对我来说，这感觉像是一个重温过去 250 年美国历史的机会，我们在我与 Ken Burns 合作的其他项目中对此进行了探索——爵士乐的历史，尤其是棒球的历史——我们提出一个话题、一个想法，然后通过这个镜头来审视所有美国历史。感觉以前没有人这样做过，我们解决犯罪的方式、惩罚的方式以及我们的方式——为什么我们有监狱，为什么我们以如此高的比例监禁，所有这些事情都不是凭空而来的。我想了解我们是如何到达这里的，而做到这一点的唯一方法就是回到起点并跟随面包屑，可以说，无论它们会带向哪里。
戴维斯：你知道，回到殖民时代，对犯罪的惩罚通常是体罚，而且是相当公开的。那时，一个普通公民在他或她一生中的某个时候亲眼目睹处决的可能性有多大？
诺维克：是的。我很惊讶地从我们的一些学者和专家那里得知，在美国殖民地，对各种犯罪行为执行死刑是很常见的。不仅仅是我们今天所认为的非常严重的暴力犯罪——谋杀、强奸等——而且你也可能因入室盗窃、通奸、亵渎、抢劫等罪而被判处死刑——这些罪行种类繁多。据我们了解，美国殖民地的大多数人都会在一生中的某个时刻目睹过处决。这令我震惊。
戴维斯：我的意思是，这是因为他们相信这会阻止犯罪，还是只是对这些公开处决有这样的兴趣？
诺维克：我认为答案是两者兼而有之——我们一直对那些违法者、不遵守规则以及被抓住并必须付出代价的人着迷。所以这就是——而且这不仅仅是美国人。人类总是对谁是不法之徒、罪犯以及他们为什么要做那样的事情感兴趣？我们希望看到他们受到惩罚。

我认为，为什么公开实施惩罚，部分是为了威慑——这就是想法——羞辱，只是向每个人传递一个关于国家权力的信息。所以，我认为，它的作用是将社会结构结合在一起，建立社区，这就是我们作为一个社区对那些违反我们规则的人所做的事情。但事实证明，它也可能对所有这些事情产生某种破坏性影响。一大群人可能会聚集在处决现场，他们可能会开始煽动暴民，甚至可能会发生骚乱，人们可能会在对处决感到兴奋的过程中受伤或被抢劫。他们可能会认同被处死的人，并认为这是不公正的。
因此，到了革命时期，我们的一些开国元勋们开始提出这样的想法：这种公开惩罚及其野蛮性质实际上对整个社会不利，我们应该想出一种更好的方法来做到这一点。
戴维斯：对。体罚的一种替代方法是监禁，这会导致我们入狱。早期的监狱是什么样的？

title_en: Exclusive: White House requires signoff before staffers testify to Congress
title_zh: 独家：白宫要求工作人员在国会作证前签字
summary: The White House counsel has instructed all executive branch agencies to get permission from their chief legal counsel and legislative affairs offices before allowing any employee to testify before Congress, according to a memo obtained by Axios. Why it matters
summary_zh: 白宫法律顾问已指示所有行政部门机构获得首席法律顾问和立法事务办公室的许可
body_en: The White House counsel has instructed all executive branch agencies to get permission from their chief legal counsel and legislative affairs offices before allowing any employee to testify before Congress, according to a memo obtained by Axios.

Why it matters: Monday's memo from White House Counsel Will Scharf is the latest sign President Trump is ready to fight the many investigations being promised by Democrats, who will have significant majorities in both chambers of Congress in January.
"The Trump administration will not be extorted, intimidated, or threatened into submission by politically motivated baseless investigations," a White House official said.

Zoom in: Scharf's memo to staffers follows a letter he sent last week to the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif). In that letter, Scharf warned Democrats to limit their investigations to "legitimate" inquiries.
"The Supreme Court has held that '[i]nvestigations conducted solely for the personal aggrandizement of the investigators or to 'punish ' those investigated are indefensible," Scharf warned.

"Congressional investigations must further a legitimate legislative task; Congress cannot employ them to exercise powers of criminal prosecution assigned to the Executive and the Judiciary," the letter said.

Between the lines: Partisans will likely differ on what's "legitimate," but it's clear that Scharf's office will use its interpretation in deciding whether to allow executive branch employees to testify.

"We are ready to engage with Congress," the White House official said, "This process ensures reasonable requests are respected, but baseless political attempts to undermine our mission will not be accepted as the status quo by Democrats' who want to slow the administration down from its historic work."

In his Monday memo, Scharf said the administration "will remain disciplined in pursuing the work and service the American people deserve by ensuring that all Executive Departments and Agencies follow the established White House consultation process ... before any agency personnel may agree to appear before any congressional committee."
Zoom out: For more than a year, Trump's administration has planned for the day congressional investigations ramp up.
Trump knows he also faces the prospect of impeachment. But advisers say that's no longer threatening to Trump, and he doesn't believe there would be the 67 votes needed in the Senate to remove him.
"The president can count, and he won't be cowed," a Trump adviser said.
Trump also has promised to pre-emptively pardon staffers and allies he believes will be unfairly targeted by Congress or prosecutors in future Democratic administrations.
body_zh: 根据 Axios 获得的一份备忘录，白宫法律顾问已指示所有行政部门机构在允许任何员工在国会作证之前必须获得首席法律顾问和立法事务办公室的许可。
为什么重要：白宫法律顾问威尔·沙夫周一的备忘录是特朗普总统准备对抗民主党承诺的多项调查的最新迹象，民主党将在一月份在国会参众两院占据绝大多数席位。
一名白宫官员表示：“特朗普政府不会因出于政治动机的毫无根据的调查而被勒索、恐吓或威胁屈服。”
放大：沙夫在写给工作人员的备忘录之前，他上周向即将上任的众议院监督委员会主席、众议员罗伯特·加西亚（加利福尼亚州民主党人）发出了一封信。沙夫在那封信中警告民主党人将调查范围限制在“合法”调查范围内。
沙夫警告说：“最高法院认为，‘纯粹为了调查人员个人利益或‘惩罚’被调查者而进行的调查是站不住脚的。”
信中说：“国会的调查必须推进合法的立法任务；国会不能利用它们来行使分配给行政和司法部门的刑事起诉权。”
言外之意是：党派可能对什么是“合法”存在分歧，但很明显，沙夫办公室将利用其解释来决定是否允许行政部门员工作证。
这位白宫官员表示：“我们已准备好与国会接触，这一程序可确保合理的要求得到尊重，但破坏我们使命的毫无根据的政治企图不会被民主党人接受为现状，因为他们希望减缓政府的历史性工作。”
沙夫在周一的备忘录中表示，政府“将继续遵守纪律，追求美国人民应得的工作和服务，确保所有行政部门和机构遵循既定的白宫协商程序……在任何机构人员同意出席任何国会委员会之前。”
缩小范围：一年多来，特朗普政府一直在计划国会调查的那一天。
特朗普知道他也面临着弹劾的前景。但顾问们表示，这不再对特朗普构成威胁，而且他认为参议院不会获得罢免他所需的 67 票。
特朗普的一名顾问表示：“总统会计算，他不会被吓倒。”
特朗普还承诺先发制人地赦免他认为在未来民主党政府中将成为国会或检察官不公平攻击目标的工作人员和盟友。

title_en: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
title_zh: 林赛·克兰西 (Lindsay Clancy) 因杀害儿童罪名将于 2027 年春季接受新审判
summary: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.
summary_zh: 马萨诸塞州对林赛·克兰西进行了新的审判，检察官寻求对杀害她三个年幼的孩子的刑事定罪。
body_en: Lindsay Clancy and her attorney Kevin Reddington listen as Judge William Sullivan declares a mistrial at the conclusion of Clancy's murder trial at the Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., on Sept. 4. Greg Derr/POOL/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Prosecutors are seeking a new trial for Lindsay Clancy in the deaths of her three children. The trial is scheduled to begin on March 29, 2027.

There had been speculation that the mistrial of her first trial might spur prosecutors to consider lesser charges that wouldn't require a jury, such as manslaughter or second-degree murder. But no changes to the charges were made in Monday's court hearing.
"Given what the charges are, it requires a jury trial," Assistant District Attorney Jennifer Sprague told Judge William Sullivan in Plymouth, Mass.

In response, Clancy's defense attorney Kevin Reddington stated, "I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments."
The Lindsay Clancy case ends in a mistrial. Where might it go from here?
Judge Sullivan is expected to preside over the new trial. He oversaw Clancy's murder trial that ended in a mistrial two months ago.
The decision to retry Clancy emerges after the judge denied a request from Clancy's defense team to dismiss the criminal charges against her on double jeopardy grounds.
Clancy's defense has argued that she shouldn't be held criminally responsible for killing her young children because she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis.

Clancy was initially tried on three charges of first-degree murder, one for each of her children. Her case has drawn intense media interest, due to the shocking killings of her young children. And as WBUR has reported , the trial has also sparked conspiracy theories online.

Sullivan declared a mistrial on Sept. 4, after five weeks of testimony and seven days of jury deliberations. The jurors, nine women and three men, repeatedly told Sullivan they were deadlocked , unable to reach a unanimous decision. Jurors said a lone juror refused to join 11 others in finding Clancy not guilty of murder.
Lindsay Clancy's trial highlights gaps in understanding, treating postpartum psychosis

Clancy's defense filed several motions after the mistrial. The first asked the court to issue a "required finding of not guilty," a Massachusetts state law term for instances where judges determine there's insufficient evidence to sustain a conviction. Another focused on the holdout juror, asking the court for an inquiry and to examine their responses to a juror questionnaire and other records. Sullivan denied both of those motions .

When deliberations were dragging out at the end of the trial, Reddington had asked the judge to remove the holdout juror, saying the jury foreperson reported one juror refused to follow the law in regards to reasonable doubt. Sullivan declined to dismiss the juror, saying he reaffirmed his instructions with all the jurors about the law.
Tragic case highlights postpartum mental health

Clancy, 36, did not testify during the trial. But her attorneys didn't deny that she killed her three children in January of 2023. Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, were found strangled in the basement of the home Clancy shared with her then-husband Patrick in Duxbury, Mass., south of Boston.

In court, Clancy's defense argued that she can't be held criminally liable because of her mental state at the time of the killings. Her attorney said Clancy was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis, and didn't get adequate mental health help when she sought it out.
"I'm appalled and disgusted," Reddington said of Clancy's medical care, as NPR and WBUR reported . "It's repulsive what happened here."

But prosecutors argued Clancy was mentally capable of committing a premeditated crime, accusing her of sending her husband out on errands so she would be alone with their children. And they raised doubts about Clancy's claims that a voice told her to kill them.
body_zh: 9 月 4 日，马萨诸塞州普利茅斯县高等法院，威廉·沙利文法官宣布克兰西谋杀案审判无效，林赛·克兰西和她的律师凯文·雷丁顿在听。格雷格·德尔/POOL/法新社，盖蒂图片社 隐藏标题栏
检察官正在寻求对林赛·克兰西三个孩子的死亡进行新的审判。审判定于 2027 年 3 月 29 日开始。
有人猜测，她的第一次审判的误审可能会促使检察官考虑不需要陪审团的较轻指控，例如过失杀人或二级谋杀。但周一的法庭听证会没有对指控做出任何改变。
“鉴于指控的内容，需要陪审团审判，”助理地方检察官詹妮弗·斯普拉格在马萨诸塞州普利茅斯告诉法官威廉·沙利文。
作为回应，克兰西的辩护律师凯文·雷丁顿表示：“我认为你可以从字里行间看出，当他们说此案需要陪审团时，这是地方检察官的间接评论，他们打算继续进行一级谋杀起诉。”
林赛·克兰西案以无效审判告终。它可能会走向何方？
沙利文法官预计将主持新的审判。他监督了克兰西谋杀案的审判，该审判在两个月前以无效审判告终。
在法官拒绝了克兰西辩护团队以双重危险为由驳回对她的刑事指控的请求后，决定重审克兰西。
克兰西的辩护律师辩称，她不应该因杀害年幼的孩子而承担刑事责任，因为她患有严重的产后精神病。
克兰西最初因三项一级谋杀罪受审，每人一项针对她的孩子。由于她年幼的孩子遭到令人震惊的杀害，她的案件引起了媒体的强烈关注。正如 WBUR 报道的那样，该审判还在网上引发了阴谋论。
经过五周的作证和陪审团七天的审议后，沙利文于 9 月 4 日宣布审判无效。陪审员（九名女性和三名男性）反复告诉沙利文，他们陷入僵局，无法达成一致决定。陪审员表示，一名陪审员拒绝与其他 11 名陪审员一起裁定克兰西无谋杀罪。
林赛·克兰西的试验凸显了理解和治疗产后精神病方面的差距
克兰西的辩方在无效审判后提出了几项动议。第一个要求法院发布“必要的无罪判决”，这是马萨诸塞州的法律术语，指的是法官确定没有足够证据维持定罪的情况。另一项针对的是坚持抵制的陪审员，要求法院进行调查并检查他们对陪审员调查问卷和其他记录的回答。沙利文否认了这两项动议。
当审判结束时审议拖延时，雷丁顿要求法官罢免拒不服从的陪审员，称陪审团主席报告称，一名陪审员拒绝遵守有关合理怀疑的法律。沙利文拒绝解雇陪审员，称他向所有陪审员重申了有关法律的指示。
悲惨案例凸显产后心理健康
36 岁的克兰西在审判期间没有作证。但她的律师并没有否认她在 2023 年 1 月杀害了自己的三个孩子。5 岁的科拉、3 岁的道森和 8 个月大的卡兰被发现被勒死在克兰西与当时的丈夫帕特里克位于波士顿南部马萨诸塞州达克斯伯里的家的地下室里。
在法庭上，克兰西的辩护律师辩称，由于杀人时她的精神状态，她不能被追究刑事责任。她的律师表示，克兰西患有严重的产后精神病，当她寻求治疗时并没有得到足够的心理健康帮助。
据 NPR 和 WBUR 报道，雷丁顿在谈到克兰西的医疗护理时表示：“我感到震惊和厌恶。” “这里发生的事情令人厌恶。”
但检察官辩称，克兰西在精神上有能力实施有预谋的犯罪，并指控她派丈夫出去办事，这样她就可以单独和孩子们在一起。他们对克兰西声称有声音告诉她杀死他们的说法表示怀疑。

body_en: Mayor axes strategic response group that cracked down on protesters and announces new community safety division

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, announced Monday that he was disbanding a city police unit that has faced criticism over the years from civil rights groups who have accused it of using excessive force and unduly aggressive tactics against protesters.

In a video released Monday morning, Mamdani said the move stemmed from a campaign pledge he made to disband the New York City police department’s strategic response group (SRG). “Today, we are keeping that promise,” Mamdani said in the video.

An accompanying joint statement from Mamdani and NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch said the overhaul would “transform how the city prepares for and responds to protests, placing communication, de-escalation and civilian coordination at the center of our approach, while protecting New Yorkers’ constitutional right to protest”.
Mamdani’s influence sharply felt as Democrats win big in affordability election

Along with eliminating the SRG, which was founded in 2015 ostensibly to focus on counter-terrorism, Mamdani and Tisch’s statement also said that the city planned to establish a “first-of-its-kind, civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD)” within the mayor’s office of community safety.
That division will not have weapons or arrest powers, unlike the SRG, according to the announcement.

The city will also establish what they described as a “specialized dialogue team” that will be known as the “First Amendment Support Team” (Fast) within the NYPD’s community affairs bureau, Mamdani and Tisch’s statement said. The creation of Fast is meant to “improve the NYPD’s protest response”, and it will consist of 30 uniformed officers trained in communication and de-escalation, the mayor and police commissioner said.
Additionally, their statement said, the NYPD will create a new patrol support division (PSD) within its patrol services bureau.
Plans call for the unit to be staffed with vetted officers who will primarily perform patrol-related duties and receive specialized crowd management training to support responses to demonstrations.

The reforms also introduce “significant new restrictions on the tactics and weapons” officers can use during protests and demonstrations – banning irritant gas, kettling and long guns. Responding officers will no longer be allowed to deploy pepper spray “as a crowd-management tool” – and “long-range acoustic devices” meant to affect protesters’ hearing “will be limited to 90 decibels”, Mamdani and Tisch said in their statement.

Under the new structure, the mayor said, the SRG’s counter-terrorism functions – “including heavy weapons deployments at critical infrastructure” – will be consolidated within the NYPD’s intelligence and counter-terrorism bureau.

The statement said that helped ensure a complete separation between the city’s counter-terrorism operations and protests protected by the rights to free speech and assembly guaranteed by the US constitution’s first amendment.

Tisch said that the new structure was “designed to consolidate our counterterrorism capabilities, provide greater support to our patrol officers and ensure we continue to respond to protests consistent with public safety and the first amendment”.
“These changes will make us a stronger, more effective department,” she said.
The administration said that the SRG-related reforms come at “no additional cost and without increasing or reducing NYPD headcount”.
While civil rights groups hailed Monday’s announcement, the New York Police Benevolent Association’s president, Patrick Hendry, criticized it in a statement on social media.

“Today is not a good day for New Yorkers who just want a safe and orderly city,” said the statement from Hendry, whose organization is a labor union representing more than 21,000 active NYPD officers. “Mayor Mamdani is showing his true colors: he’s willing to put your safety and police officers’ safety at risk to appease his radical base.
“So the next time your life is disrupted by demonstrators who are blocking bridges and roadways or causing chaos on our streets, remember: Mayor Mamdani is on their side, not yours.”
body_zh: 市长解散镇压抗议者的战略反应小组，并宣布新的社区安全部门
纽约市市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼周一宣布，他将解散一支城市警察部队，该部队多年来一直受到民权组织的批评，这些组织指责该部队对抗议者使用过度武力和过度激进的策略。
在周一早上发布的视频中，马姆达尼表示此举源于他在竞选时做出的解散纽约市警察局战略响应小组（SRG）的承诺。 “今天，我们兑现了这一承诺，”马姆达尼在视频中说道。
马姆达尼和纽约警察局局长杰西卡·蒂什发表的联合声明表示，此次改革将“改变该市准备和应对抗议活动的方式，将沟通、降级和民间协调置于我们方法的中心，同时保护纽约人的宪法抗议权利”。
随着民主党在负担能力选举中大获全胜，马姆达尼的影响力急剧增强
Mamdani 和 Tisch 的声明还表示，除了撤销 2015 年成立、表面上专注于反恐的 SRG 外，该市还计划在市长社区安全办公室内设立一个“首个由平民领导的社区对话和降级部门 (CDDD)”。
公告称，与 SRG 不同，该部门不会拥有武器或逮捕权。
马姆达尼和蒂什的声明称，该市还将在纽约市警察局社区事务局内建立一个他们所说的“专门对话小组”，即“第一修正案支持小组”（快速）。市长和警察局长表示，Fast 的成立旨在“改善纽约市警察局的抗议反应”，该小组将由 30 名接受过沟通和降级培训的穿制服的警察组成。
此外，他们的声明称，纽约警察局将在其巡逻服务局内设立一个新的巡逻支持部门（PSD）。
计划要求该单位配备经过审查的警官，他们将主要履行巡逻相关职责，并接受专门的人群管理培训，以支持应对示威活动。
改革还对警察在抗议和示威期间可以使用的“战术和武器进行了重大新限制”——禁止使用刺激性气体、水壶和长枪。马姆达尼和蒂什在声明中表示，响应警察将不再被允许使用胡椒喷雾“作为人群管理工具”，而旨在影响抗议者听力的“远程声学装置”“将被限制在 90 分贝”。
市长表示，在新的结构下，SRG 的反恐职能——“包括在关键基础设施部署重型武器”——将整合到纽约警察局的情报和反恐局内。
声明称，这有助于确保该市的反恐行动与抗议活动完全分开，而抗议活动受到美国宪法第一修正案保障的言论和集会自由权的保护。
蒂施表示，新结构的目的“旨在巩固我们的反恐能力，为我们的巡逻人员提供更大的支持，并确保我们继续根据公共安全和第一修正案对抗议活动做出反应”。
“这些变化将使我们成为一个更强大、更有效的部门，”她说。
政府表示，与 SRG 相关的改革“不会产生额外成本，也不会增加或减少纽约警察局的人数”。
尽管民权组织对周一的声明表示欢迎，但纽约警察慈善协会主席帕特里克·亨德利在社交媒体上的一份声明中对此提出了批评。
亨德利的声明表示：“对于只想要一个安全有序的城市的纽约人来说，今天不是好日子。”亨德利的组织是一个工会，代表着 21,000 多名在职纽约警察局官员。 “马姆达尼市长露出了他的真面目：他愿意将你和警察的安全置于危险之中，以安抚他的激进派选民。
“因此，下次当你的生活被示威者堵塞桥梁和道路或在街道上制造混乱时，请记住：马姆达尼市长站在他们一边，而不是你一边。”

title_en: Passing bill to speed up gas projects and datacenters would be ‘serious mistake’, Al Gore says
title_zh: 戈尔表示，通过加速天然气项目和数据中心的法案将是“严重错误”
summary: Former US vice-president at Cop31 urges lawmakers to rethink contentious bipartisan Baaja bill advanced by the US Senate It would be a “serious mistake” to pass a contentious bipartisan bill to speed up energy projects and datacenters that has divided Democrat
summary_zh: 美国前副主席在第31次缔约方会议上敦促立法者重新考虑美国参议院提出的有争议的两党巴哈法案，这将是一个“严重的错误”
body_en: Former US vice-president at Cop31 urges lawmakers to rethink contentious bipartisan Baaja bill advanced by the US Senate
It would be a “serious mistake” to pass a contentious bipartisan bill to speed up energy projects and datacenters that has divided Democrats and environmentalists, Al Gore said.

The legislation, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (Baaja), will make it easier to build large infrastructure projects in the US, from oil and gas pipelines and datacenters to crucial clean energy components such as solar and wind power and transmission lines, scaling back environmental protections and legal challenges in order to do so.

The permitting bill, devised by a group of Republicans and Democrats, passed a procedural vote in the US Senate last week , but has split Democrats and green groups over whether its trade-offs are worth supporting. Gore, the former US vice-president, said he is opposed to the bill and urged a rethink.

“I think it would be a serious mistake, particularly in the wake of the astonishing election results last week,” Gore, referencing Democrats’ sweeping midterm wins , said at the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey.

“The fact that President Trump endorsed it enthusiastically is a clue, the fact that the American Petroleum Institute is giving out free tacos in Washington to support it is also a clue. I hope they reconsider because I think it would be a very, very serious mistake.”

Trump, who has repeatedly attempted to halt clean energy projects in the US, said last week wind turbines are a “major loser” and that he will prevent any more being built, even as the bill to sweep away blockages to clean energy is being considered.

“Trump will implement any legislation given to him in a way that continues to redeem his unethical pledge to the fossil fuel industry during his campaign,” Gore said, referencing Trump’s promise to provide help to oil and gas executives in return for donations prior to the 2024 election .

“The president of the United States is in charge of implementing whatever legislation is passed and he doesn’t play by the rules, he doesn’t respect the law and it’s not a mystery how he would try to implement this legislation,” Gore said. “It would lock in a lot of new pipelines and fossil fuel facilities. And we will have a chance with the new Congress and the new balance of power in the US government to do a much better job.”

But while Democrats will be able to craft a far more renewables-friendly permitting bill when they gain control of Congress in January, proponents of Baaja point out that support from Trump and Republicans will likely wither, meaning there will be no legislation at all to help stop wind and solar projects being bogged down in lengthy reviews, with new generation struggling to bring clean electricity to Americans due to a lack of transmission lines across the country.
A final Senate vote is expected this week and if that passes it would move to the House.
Sheldon Whitehouse, a Democratic senator and longtime climate advocate who helped craft the bill, said he was working to improve the legislation but rejected Gore’s criticism.

“Mr Gore neither spoke to Senator [Martin] Heinrich or me or our teams before he reached that conclusion,” Whitehouse, who is also at Cop31 , said. Whitehouse said he was working on “a variety of amendments to see what can be done to shore up potential holes in the bill” including provisions that would prevent Trump from arbitrarily blocking clean energy developments.

“There was a huge surge of misinformation that came kind of immediately after the text was released … we have had lots of exaggerated fears,” Whitehouse added about the criticism of the bill from some Democrats and green groups that environmental protections were being gutted for a modest reduction in greenhouse gas pollution.
The bill could result in as much as 1.5bn tons of emissions reductions by 2040, according to one analysis , and Whitehouse said he hoped amendments would increase this total.

Whether or not this is enough pollution reduction to justify environmental rollbacks has cut to the heart of tension in the broader green movement over whether to prioritize the climate crisis even if this means all sorts of new infrastructure that may impact ecosystems and communities.
“The prospect of losing tools to slow down and stop the cruelest projects should be haunting everyone,” said Abigail Dillen, president of Earthjustice, which opposes Baaja.

For Whitehouse, though, tackling the climate crisis is paramount. “Nothing is going to be more devastating to the environment than continuing on our pace of climate change, by like a factor of 100,” he said.

“Clean energy development is wildly outpacing fossil fuel development now. In the old days the developers were almost always the bad guys and a mindset developed around that pattern,” the senator added.
body_zh: 第 31 届缔约方大会上的美国前副主席敦促立法者重新考虑美国参议院提出的有争议的两党巴哈法案
戈尔表示，通过一项有争议的两党法案来加快能源项目和数据中心的建设将是一个“严重的错误”，该法案已经引起了民主党和环保人士的分歧。
这项名为《美国两党负担能力和就业法案》(Baaja) 的立法将使在美国建设大型基础设施项目变得更加容易，从石油和天然气管道和数据中心到太阳能和风能和输电线路等关键的清洁能源组件，从而减少环境保护和法律挑战。
这项由共和党和民主党共同制定的许可法案上周在美国参议院通过了程序性投票，但在其权衡是否值得支持的问题上，民主党和绿党产生了分歧。美国前副总统戈尔表示，他反对该法案，并敦促重新考虑。
戈尔在土耳其安塔利亚举行的第 31 届缔约方会议气候峰会上提到民主党在中期选举中取得压倒性胜利时表示，“我认为这将是一个严重的错误，尤其是在上周选举结果令人震惊之后。”
“特朗普总统热情支持这一事实就是一条线索，美国石油学会在华盛顿免费发放玉米饼来支持这一事实也是一条线索。我希望他们重新考虑，因为我认为这将是一个非常非常严重的错误。”
曾多次试图叫停美国清洁能源项目的特朗普上周表示，风力涡轮机是“主要输家”，他将阻止更多风力涡轮机的建设，尽管正在考虑消除清洁能源障碍的法案。
戈尔表示：“特朗普将执行赋予他的任何立法，以继续兑现他在竞选期间对化石燃料行业做出的不道德承诺。”他指的是特朗普承诺在 2024 年大选前向石油和天然气高管提供帮助，以换取捐款。
戈尔说：“美国总统负责执行通过的任何立法，但他不遵守规则，不尊重法律，他将如何尝试执行这项立法并不神秘。” “这将锁定大量新的管道和化石燃料设施。我们将有机会在新国会和美国政府新的权力平衡下做得更好。”
不过，虽然民主党在一月份获得国会控制权后将能够制定一项对可再生能源更加友好的许可法案，但巴哈的支持者指出，特朗普和共和党的支持可能会减弱，这意味着根本不会有任何立法来帮助阻止风能和太阳能项目陷入漫长的审查，而由于全国范围内缺乏输电线路，新一代人很难为美国人提供清洁电力。
预计参议院将于本周进行最终投票，如果通过，将移交众议院。
帮助起草该法案的民主党参议员、长期气候倡导者谢尔登·怀特豪斯表示，他正在努力改进立法，但拒绝了戈尔的批评。
“在得出这一结论之前，戈尔先生没有与参议员[马丁]海因里希、我或我们的团队交谈，”也是 Cop31 成员的怀特豪斯说。白宫表示，他正在制定“各种修正案，看看可以采取哪些措施来弥补该法案中的潜在漏洞”，其中包括防止特朗普任意阻止清洁能源开发的条款。
“该文本发布后，错误信息立即大量涌现……我们有很多夸大的恐惧，”怀特豪斯补充道，一些民主党人和绿色团体对该法案提出批评，称环境保护正在因适度减少温室气体污染而遭到破坏。
一项分析显示，到 2040 年，该法案可能会减少多达 15 亿吨的排放量，白宫表示，他希望修正案能够增加这一总量。
这是否足以减少污染以证明环境倒退的合理性，已经成为更广泛的绿色运动中紧张局势的核心，即是否优先考虑气候危机，即使这意味着可能影响生态系统和社区的各种新基础设施。
“失去减缓和阻止最残酷项目的工具的前景应该困扰着每个人，”反对巴哈的地球正义组织主席阿比盖尔·迪伦说。
不过，对于白宫来说，应对气候危机至关重要。 “没有什么比继续以 100 倍的速度应对气候变化对环境造成的破坏更大的了，”他说。
“现在清洁能源的发展远远超过了化石燃料的发展。在过去，开发商几乎总是坏人，并且围绕这种模式形成了一种心态，”这位参议员补充道。

title_en: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
title_zh: 克里斯·范·霍伦说他可以击败查克·舒默。这是他的案例
summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.
summary_zh: 参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 告诉 NPR 早间版，为什么他相信自己能够击败参议员查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer)，以及他将改变参议院民主党法案的哪些内容
body_en: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer for Senate leader : NPR

Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer for Senate leader Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.
Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., on his challenge for Senate majority leader
Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader

Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Monday that he is gaining momentum in his bid to unseat longtime Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, taking a traditionally private Senate leadership contest into public view.
"Well, I'm the underdog, but we are really moving in the right direction here," Van Hollen told NPR's Steve Inskeep on Morning Edition .

Over the weekend, he appeared on CNN, ABC and Fox News to make his case for new Democratic leadership after his party's sweeping midterm victories. Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, says he has enough votes to remain leader.
How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front

Van Hollen is hardly a Washington outsider. The progressive Democrat has spent nearly 25 years on Capitol Hill, served as a deputy to then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and led Democratic campaign efforts in both chambers. He has been a vocal opponent of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown and dismantling of the U.S. Agency for International Development, and he has called for investigations into the administration's foreign aid cuts.

Schumer has continued to support U.S. military assistance to Israel despite his criticism of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Van Hollen, by contrast, has pushed to restrict weapons sales and military aid to the Israeli government over its war in Gaza, while pressing for more humanitarian aid to Palestinians.
"I certainly oppose the idea of an American taxpayer blank check to the government of Israel, regardless of its actions," Van Hollen said.
Van Hollen also wants Democratic leaders to stay out of contested primaries. He pointed to the victories of incoming Sens. Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota.
"We have two senators-elect who would not be there if the current majority leader had his way," he said.
He described the midterm victories as a populist rejection of President Trump, rather than an election orchestrated by Washington Democrats.
What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
Van Hollen also cited legislation to strengthen labor unions, which never received a vote on the Senate floor. On the war in Iran, he called for an end to further funding.
"We should not be voting for one penny in mid-December to continue this war," he said.

Van Hollen will need close to 30 votes, a simple majority of the Senate Democratic caucus, to win. The election will be decided by secret ballot behind closed doors, making it difficult to know how many votes either candidate secured.

body_zh: 克里斯·范·霍伦表示他可以击败查克·舒默成为参议院领袖：NPR
克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 表示，他可以击败查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 竞选参议院领袖。克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 告诉 NPR 早间版，为什么他相信自己可以击败参议员查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer)，以及他将改变参议院民主党领导层。
马里兰州民主党参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 挑战参议院多数党领袖
克里斯·范霍伦表示，他将挑战查克·舒默竞选参议院多数党领袖
马里兰州参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 周一表示，他正在努力推翻长期担任民主党领袖的查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer)，将传统上不公开的参议院领导权竞争带入公众视野。
“好吧，我是失败者，但我们确实正在朝着正确的方向前进，”范·霍伦在早间版节目中告诉 NPR 的史蒂夫·英斯基普。
周末，他出现在美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN)、美国广播公司 (ABC) 和福克斯新闻频道上，为民主党在中期选举中取得压倒性胜利后为新的民主党领导层辩护。领导参议院民主党近十年的舒默表示，他有足够的选票来保持领导地位。
参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 计划如何在对外援助方面展示民主党的权力
范霍伦并不是华盛顿的局外人。这位进步的民主党人在国会山工作了近 25 年，担任时任众议院议长南希·佩洛西 (Nancy Pelosi) 的副手，并领导了参众两院的民主党竞选活动。他一直强烈反对特朗普政府镇压移民和解散美国国际开发署，并呼吁对政府削减对外援助的行为进行调查。
尽管舒默批评总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡，但他继续支持美国对以色列的军事援助。相比之下，范霍伦则因加沙战争而推动限制向以色列政府出售武器和提供军事援助，同时敦促向巴勒斯坦人提供更多人道主义援助。
范霍伦说：“我当然反对向以色列政府发放美国纳税人空白支票的想法，无论以色列政府采取什么行动。”
范霍伦还希望民主党领导人不要参与竞争激烈的初选。他指出了即将上任的密歇根州参议员阿卜杜勒·赛义德和明尼苏达州参议员佩吉·弗拉纳根的胜利。
他说：“如果现任多数党领袖按他的方式行事，我们有两名当选参议员，他们就不会出席。”
他将中期选举的胜利描述为民粹主义对特朗普总统的拒绝，而不是华盛顿民主党精心策划的选举。
特朗普现在对伊朗的战略是什么？保持事物原样
范霍伦还引用了加强工会的立法，该立法从未在参议院获得投票。关于伊朗战争，他呼吁停止进一步提供资金。
“我们不应该在 12 月中旬投票一分钱来继续这场战争，”他说。
范霍伦需要获得近 30 票，即参议院民主党核心小组的简单多数票才能获胜。选举将通过闭门无记名投票方式决定，因此很难知道两位候选人获得了多少票。

title_en: Lindsay Clancy to be retried on first-degree murder charges in March
title_zh: 林赛·克兰西 (Lindsay Clancy) 将于三月因一级谋杀罪重审
summary: Prosecutors plan to retry Lindsay Clancy on first-degree murder charges, after her first Massachusetts murder trial ended in a mistrial.
summary_zh: 在林赛·克兰西在马萨诸塞州的第一次谋杀案审判以误审结束后，检察官计划以一级谋杀罪重审她。
body_en: Prosecutors plan to retry Lindsay Clancy on first-degree murder charges, after her first Massachusetts murder trial ended in a mistrial. The judge set a jury trial date for March 29, 2027.

Clancy was back in Plymouth Superior Court Monday morning as prosecutors addressed how they plan to proceed with her case in what was a brief but tense hearing . The commonwealth argued for a later trial date in May, citing other cases on the docket, but Judge William Sullivan, who is retiring in June 2027, was firm in seeking a March date.

Clancy was charged with first-degree murder in the deaths of her three children in their Duxbury home on Jan. 24, 2023. In her first trial, Clancy's attorney admitted she killed 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan, but argued that she was not criminally responsible because she was overmedicated and suffering from postpartum psychosis.
Prosecutors said Clancy knew right from wrong and planned to strangle her children. The jury ended up deadlocked and a mistrial was declared on Sept. 4.
Judge Sullivan has already made a number of rulings since the last hearing in the case on Nov. 9, when he denied Clancy's motion to dismiss the murder charges.

Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz has the power to decide to retry Clancy on first-degree murder charges again, which would require another jury trial. Cruz, who was not in court Monday, could also have tried Clancy on a lesser charge, such as second-degree murder or manslaughter.

Clancy's attorney Kevin Reddington has said in the past that he would never accept a plea deal that puts her in jail at all. If Clancy was re-tried on lesser charges she would have had the choice to have either a judge or a jury decide the outcome of this case.

Reddington said Monday he plans to once again request that the trial is split in two - one trial to prove guilt and another to prove her mental state at the time. That request was denied by Judge Sullivan last time.

"It's not guilty. They still have to prove that their investigation - using the term loosely - proved that she's guilty," Reddington said. "The jury then has to look at the issue of criminal responsibility or lack thereof, which is very, very strong for the defense."
WBZ-TV legal analyst Jennifer Roman said the prosecution's choice to pursue first-degree murder charges again does not come as a surprise.

"They came out pretty strongly after the first trial that they wanted justice for these three children, and the prosecution has made it clear that justice for them is a conviction on first-degree murder," she said.
Roman said the prosecution "needs to do a better job of telling their narrative this time around."

"I think that's where they fell short the first time and it hurt them ultimately when we had this hung jury," she said. "I think they really need to be clear as to what the theory of their case is, right from the outset."
Finding another jury for Clancy's second trial will not be easy, Roman said.

"This has gotten national, worldwide coverage. Everybody has heard of this case, even if they didn't follow the trial, they've certainly heard about it now," she said. "I think we are going to see an extended jury empanelment period of time for them to get the 14 or 15 members of that jury pool."
The next status hearing in the case is scheduled for Dec. 30.

body_zh: 在林赛·克兰西在马萨诸塞州的第一次谋杀案审判以误审结束后，检察官计划以一级谋杀罪重审她。法官将陪审团审判日期定为 2027 年 3 月 29 日。
周一早上，克兰西回到普利茅斯高等法院，检察官在简短但紧张的听证会上讨论了他们计划如何处理她的案件。联邦政府援引待审案件中的其他案件，主张将审判日期推迟到 5 月，但将于 2027 年 6 月退休的威廉·沙利文法官坚决寻求在 3 月进行审判。
2023 年 1 月 24 日，克兰西在达克斯伯里的家中杀死了她的三个孩子，被指控犯有一级谋杀罪。在第一次审判中，克兰西的律师承认她杀死了 5 岁的科拉、3 岁的道森和 8 个月大的卡兰，但辩称她不需承担刑事责任，因为她服药过量并患有产后精神病。
检察官表示，克兰西知道是非，并计划勒死她的孩子。陪审团最终陷入僵局，并于 9 月 4 日宣布无效审判。
自11月9日该案上次听证会以来，沙利文法官已经做出了多项裁决，当时他驳回了克兰西驳回谋杀指控的动议。
普利茅斯县地方检察官蒂姆·克鲁兹有权决定再次以一级谋杀罪重审克兰西，这将需要陪审团再次审判。克鲁兹周一没有出庭，他也可以以较轻的罪名审判克兰西，例如二级谋杀或过失杀人。
克兰西的律师凯文·雷丁顿过去曾表示，他永远不会接受将她送入监狱的认罪协议。如果克兰西以较轻的罪名重新受审，她可以选择让法官或陪审团来决定此案的结果。
雷丁顿周一表示，他计划再次要求将审判分为两部分——一项审判是为了证明她有罪，另一项审判是为了证明她当时的精神状态。沙利文法官上次拒绝了这一请求。
“她无罪。他们仍然需要证明他们的调查——宽松地使用这个词——证明她有罪，”雷丁顿说。 “然后陪审团必须考虑刑事责任或缺乏刑事责任的问题，这对辩方来说非常非常有力。”
WBZ-TV 法律分析师詹妮弗·罗曼 (Jennifer Roman) 表示，检方选择再次提起一级谋杀指控并不令人意外。
“他们在第一次审判后非常强烈地表示，他们希望为这三个孩子伸张正义，检方已明确表示，对他们的正义是对一级谋杀罪定罪，”她说。
罗曼表示，检方“这次需要更好地讲述他们的叙述”。
“我认为这就是他们第一次失败的地方，当我们的陪审团悬而未决时，这最终伤害了他们，”她说。 “我认为他们确实需要从一开始就明确他们案件的理论是什么。”
罗曼说，为克兰西的第二次审判寻找另一个陪审团并不容易。
“这件事得到了全国乃至全世界的报道。每个人都听说过这个案件，即使他们没有关注审判，但他们现在肯定也听说过，”她说。 “我认为我们将看到陪审团选任时间延长，以便他们选出 14 或 15 名陪审团成员。”
该案的下一次状态听证会定于 12 月 30 日举行。

title_en: Major U.S. banks report widespread service outages
title_zh: 美国主要银行报告大范围服务中断
summary: Customers at Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and other major financial institutions reported difficulty accessing their accounts.
summary_zh: 美国银行、摩根大通和其他主要金融机构的客户报告称难以访问其账户。
body_en: Customers at Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, U.S. Bank and other major financial institutions reported service outages on Monday, according to Downdetector.com .

Other banks seeing a spike in customer complaints about difficulty accessing their accounts included Capital One, Truist and Wells Fargo, while users also reported problems with the digital payments app Zelle, according to the outage tracker.
Chase Bank's services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday.

"Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds," a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. "We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible."

Chase also said in a social media post that a software bug in its systems affected other institutions "when we were party to a transaction involving other banks." The issue is not systemic, the bank added.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."

Bank customers started reporting problems accessing online services on Monday morning. By the afternoon, reports of outages had surged, according to Downdetector.com. As of 2 p.m. ET, nearly 4,800 users had reported problems with Chase, the most of any bank.
Chase customers reported issues accessing their online accounts, including viewing balances and performing transactions such as bank transfers and wire transfers, according to Downdetector.
Bank of America clients reported problems with ATMs as well as online and mobile banking services, according to the site.

U.S. Bank customers reported issues with their online accounts and the bank's mobile app. They also had problems transferring funds, while Wells Fargo customers reported difficulty signing in to their accounts, as well as with getting account balances and conducting transactions.

A Chase Bank customer in Texas told CBS News he tried to deposit a check at a Dallas branch early Monday, but the transaction could not be completed. A bank teller told the customer in front of him that the "system was down" without providing additional details, he added, expressing frustration at the lack of clarity about the situation.

A spokesperson for U.S. Bank said its systems were not directly impacted by the cyber outage. "However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays," the company said in a statement to CBS News.
A Capital One spokesperson said it hasn't been affected by the outage and continues to operate normally.

Zelle told CBS News its service was "operating as it should," but that some users could be experiencing issues related to problems at their financial institutions, which could be delaying Zelle payments.

"Consumers use Zelle through participating banks and credit unions, which manage their accounts and hold their funds," a Zelle spokesperson said. "Consumers do not have a separate Zelle account, and Zelle does not hold consumer funds."
Zelle's network operator, Early Warning Services, is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo.

The banking outages occurred after Microsoft restored services on Saturday following a global outage affecting its Outlook and Teams services, which disrupted users, companies and government operations worldwide. Microsoft said a technical issue caused the outage and that it was not linked to a cyberattack.

The glitches also came only days after overloaded routers forced the Federal Aviation Administration to order a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday, stranding travelers and causing thousands of canceled flights. The FAA said Sunday that airline schedules across the U.S. were returning to normal . (On Monday evening, United Airlines also said it resolved a " widespread system outage " it had been dealing with that afternoon.)
Cybersecurity experts said the root causes of the bank service disruptions, Microsoft outage and FAA system failure, while different on their face, also point to a common problem.

"Our country has seen three very serious technology incidents over the past week," Mike Chapple, an IT, analytics and operations expert at the University of Notre Dame, said in a statement to CBS News. "When we dig into the details, each one has an explanation that makes sense on its own, but they all point to a common theme: the complexity and fragility of the systems that we depend on every day."
body_zh: 据 DownDetector.com 报道，美国银行、摩根大通、合众银行和其他主要金融机构的客户周一报告服务中断。
据停电追踪公司称，其他银行的客户对账户访问困难的投诉激增，其中包括第一资本（Capital One）、Truist和富国银行（Wells Fargo），而用户也报告了数字支付应用程序Zelle的问题。
一位发言人周一表示，大通银行的服务遇到了技术错误问题，而不是网络问题。
大通发言人在一份声明中表示：“由于技术问题，一些交易需要比平常更长的时间才能完成，但客户仍然可以访问他们的账户和资金。” “我们正在努力尽快解决这个问题。”
大通银行还在社交媒体帖子中表示，“当我们参与涉及其他银行的交易时”，其系统中的软件错误影响了其他机构。该银行补充说，这个问题不是系统性的。
一些大通银行客户收到一条消息，内容是：“某些服务不可用。我们正在处理这些服务。请稍后再试。”
周一早上，银行客户开始报告访问在线服务的问题。据 DownDetector.com 称，到下午，停电报告激增。截至下午 2 点截至东部时间，近 4,800 名用户报告了大通银行的问题，是所有银行中最多的。
据 DownDetector 称，大通银行的客户报告了访问其在线账户的问题，包括查看余额和执行银行转账和电汇等交易。
据该网站称，美国银行的客户报告了 ATM 机以及在线和移动银行服务的问题。
美国银行客户报告了他们的在线账户和银行移动应用程序的问题。他们在转移资金方面也遇到了问题，而富国银行的客户则报告称，登录账户、获取账户余额和进行交易都遇到困难。
德克萨斯州的一位大通银行客户告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，他周一早些时候试图在达拉斯分行存入一张支票，但交易无法完成。他补充说，一名银行出纳员告诉他面前的客户“系统已关闭”，但没有提供更多细节，并对情况不清楚表示沮丧。
美国银行发言人表示，其系统并未受到网络中断的直接影响。该公司在给哥伦比亚广播公司新闻的一份声明中表示：“然而，尝试与其他金融机构发送或接收 Zelle 付款的客户可能会遇到交易延迟。”
第一资本发言人表示，该公司并未受到停电影响，继续正常运营。
Zelle 告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，其服务“正常运行”，但一些用户可能会遇到与金融机构问题相关的问题，这可能会延迟 Zelle 付款。
Zelle 发言人表示：“消费者通过参与银行和信用社使用 Zelle，这些银行和信用社管理他们的账户并持有他们的资金。” “消费者没有单独的Zelle账户，Zelle也不持有消费者资金。”
Zelle 的网络运营商 Early Warning Services 归美国银行、第一资本、摩根大通、PNC 银行、Truist、合众银行和富国银行等金融机构所有。
周六，微软恢复了服务，此前全球范围内的 Outlook 和 Teams 服务中断，导致全球用户、公司和政府运营中断。微软表示，此次中断是技术问题造成的，与网络攻击无关。
就在几天前，路由器超载迫使美国联邦航空管理局在周五罕见地下令在全国范围内进行地面停留，导致旅客滞留并导致数千架航班取消。美国联邦航空局周日表示，美国各地的航班时刻表已恢复正常。 （周一晚上，联合航空公司还表示，它解决了当天下午一直在处理的“大范围系统中断”问题。）
网络安全专家表示，银行服务中断、微软宕机和美国联邦航空局系统故障的根本原因虽然表面上不同，但也指向一个共同的问题。
圣母大学 IT、分析和运营专家迈克·查普尔 (Mike Chapple) 在给哥伦比亚广播公司新闻 (CBS News) 的一份声明中表示：“过去一周，我们国家发生了三起非常严重的技术事件。” “当我们深入研究细节时，每个细节都有自己合理的解释，但它们都指向一个共同的主题：我们每天依赖的系统的复杂性和脆弱性。”

title_en: Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse
title_zh: 由埃里克·特朗普支持的机器人士兵初创公司未能发放工资，可能会倒闭
summary: Robotics startup misses payroll a year after CEO used funds for luxury home.
summary_zh: 在首席执行官将资金用于豪华住宅一年后，机器人初创公司未能发放工资。
body_en: A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall. The Silicon Valley startup, Foundation Future Industries, claims it is developing and testing robots for military roles on battlefields from Ukraine to Gaza.

Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC . The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak , supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago.

This comes as Pathak and Foundation’s leadership are still looking to raise funding to support a $3 billion valuation, based on their promise to develop a humanoid robot ready for combat duty and capable of wielding various weapons.
body_zh: 据报道，由唐纳德·特朗普总统的儿子埃里克·特朗普支持和建议的一家人形机器人公司已经拖欠工资，并可能因资金短缺而濒临倒闭。硅谷初创公司未来工业基金会声称，它正在开发和测试从乌克兰到加沙战场上发挥军事作用的机器人。
匿名消息人士告诉 CNBC，基金会未能向员工支付截至 10 月 30 日的工资期工资。这家初创公司的员工尤其愤怒，因为 Foundation 的联合创始人兼首席执行官 Sankaet Pathak 据称在一年前借了 460 万美元的公司资金购买了一栋俯瞰旧金山湾的豪华住宅。
与此同时，帕塔克和基金会的领导层仍在寻求筹集资金以支持 30 亿美元的估值，因为他们承诺开发一款准备好执行战斗任务并能够使用各种武器的人形机器人。

title_en: The FAA ground stop left them stranded, so they bought a car and drove it home
title_zh: 美国联邦航空局的地面停车让他们陷入困境，所以他们买了一辆车并开回家
summary: A nationwide ground stop left Tara Harding and her employees stranded. Striking out on planes and trains, she opted to just buy an automobile.
summary_zh: 全国范围内的一次地面停留导致塔拉·哈丁和她的员工陷入困境。由于乘坐飞机和火车，她选择只买一辆汽车。
body_en: Tara Harding and her employees were at the airport trying to get home from a work trip when a nationwide ground stop left them stranded in Charlotte, North Carolina — roughly 1,600 miles from home in Bismarck, North Dakota.
She found a $48,000 solution in the form of a new Ford Bronco.

Travelers across the U.S. were left scrambling Friday when the Federal Aviation Administration announced that it was grounding all flights as it saw inconsistencies in radar data and communications. Officials said that 20,000 flights were affected in the hourslong ground stop, with 12,000 “unable to recover” after the order lifted. Thousands more flights were either delayed or canceled the next day as airlines scrambled to recover service.

Harding, a nurse practitioner who owns a clinic, was ready to get home Friday after being in town for a training with two of her employees. Her group had been at the airport for about 30 minutes when the ground stop occurred.
All three women started out trying to find options through Delta Air Lines, but flights were delayed and rebooked until they gave up the idea of getting in the air altogether, Harding said.

“In the midst of all of that, though, we’re like, ‘We should probably look at trying to get a rental car,’” Harding said. “So we were trying to look, all three of us at one time, trying to get a rental car. There was zero available rental cars within a four-hour radius.”
Overwhelmed and out of ideas, Harding called her husband to ask what she should do. He relayed to her an idea from his mom.
“She said, ‘Why don’t you guys go buy a car?’” Harding recalled.
At that point, the women had been trying unsuccessfully to rebook their flights or find alternatives for more than an hour.

So they started texting with a sales agent at a Ford dealership who promised to stay open while they waited 30 minutes for an Uber out of the Charlotte Douglas International Airport. They arrived at 7:45 p.m. and left with a new Bronco less than two hours later.
Harding said the process gave her an adrenaline rush.
“When we were leaving the airport, I was three-way calling with my husband, the car dealer and my employees, and we were looking at each other like, ‘Is this really happening right now?’” she said.
Harding said she knows it sounds “insane,” but she did what she had to do, relying on a problem-solving instinct she tied to being both an entrepreneur and a nurse.
“If it was just me, it would have probably been different,” she said. “But I had two employees that needed to get home to their children, and we had patients on Monday morning.”

Even picking a Ford Bronco was a rushed decision, she said. Harding and her husband were discussing getting a vehicle with a good resale value, but her husband suggested getting a “fun” car just in case they couldn’t sell it once she got home.
“And being a Ford girl, I was like, ‘Broncos look kind of cute and fun,’” she said.
Driving the Bronco off the lot, the women drove 27 hours nonstop to Bismarck, making the most of the trip together. They had a rotation on who would sleep and who would drive.
“We took turns napping, stopped at gas stations and drive-thrus for food,” she said.
Despite the hefty price tag, Harding said she has no regrets about her decision. The women bonded over the journey, and in the end, they have a great story to tell, she added.
As for the Bronco, Harding said it’ll be with her for the long haul.
body_zh: 塔拉·哈丁 (Tara Harding) 和她的员工出差正在机场试图回家，但全国范围内的地面停靠让他们滞留在北卡罗来纳州夏洛特，距离北达科他州俾斯麦的家大约 1,600 英里。
她找到了一个价值 48,000 美元的解决方案：一辆新的福特野马。
周五，美国联邦航空管理局宣布，由于雷达数据和通信不一致，宣布停飞所有航班，美国各地的旅客都陷入了困境。官员们表示，在长达数小时的地面停留中，有 20,000 架航班受到影响，其中 12,000 架航班在命令解除后“无法恢复”。随着航空公司争先恐后地恢复服务，第二天又有数千个航班延误或取消。
哈丁是一名拥有一家诊所的护士，她在城里与两名员工一起接受培训后，准备于周五回家。当地面停留时，她的团队已经在机场待了大约 30 分钟。
哈丁说，这三名女性一开始都试图通过达美航空寻找选择，但航班被延误并重新预订，直到她们完全放弃了乘坐飞机的想法。
“不过，在这一切之中，我们想，‘我们可能应该考虑尝试租一辆汽车，’”哈丁说。 “所以我们三个人同时试图寻找一辆租赁汽车。四小时半径内可用的租赁汽车为零。”
哈丁不知所措，不知所措，打电话给她的丈夫，询问她应该做什么。他向她转达了他妈妈的一个想法。
“她说，‘你们为什么不去买辆车呢？’”哈丁回忆道。
当时，这些女性已经尝试重新预订航班或寻找替代航班一个多小时，但没有成功。
于是，他们开始给一家福特经销店的销售代理发短信，后者承诺在他们从夏洛特道格拉斯国际机场等 30 分钟叫到 Uber 的过程中保持营业。他们于晚上 7 点 45 分抵达。不到两小时后，他开着一辆新的野马离开了。
哈丁说，这个过程让她肾上腺素激增。
“当我们离开机场时，我与我的丈夫、汽车经销商和我的员工进行了三方通话，我们面面相觑，‘这真的是现在发生的事情吗？’”她说。
哈丁说，她知道这听起来“疯狂”，但她做了她必须做的事情，依靠她作为企业家和护士所拥有的解决问题的本能。
“如果只有我，情况可能会有所不同，”她说。 “但我有两名员工需要回家照顾孩子，而且周一早上我们还有病人。”
她说，即使选择福特野马也是一个仓促的决定。哈丁和她的丈夫正在讨论购买一辆具有良好转售价值的车辆，但她的丈夫建议购买一辆“有趣”的汽车，以防万一她回家后他们无法卖掉它。
“作为一名福特女孩，我想，‘野马队看起来有点可爱又有趣，’”她说。
驾驶着 Bronco 离开停车场，两位女士不间断地开车 27 小时到达俾斯麦，充分享受了这段旅程。他们轮流决定谁睡觉、谁开车。
“我们轮流打盹，在加油站停下来，在汽车餐厅买食物，”她说。
尽管价格昂贵，哈丁表示她对自己的决定并不后悔。她补充说，这些女性在旅途中结下了不解之缘，最后，她们有一个精彩的故事要讲。
至于野马，哈丁表示它将长期陪伴她。

title_en: WATCH: 'You never notice broken windows, obviously,' Trump tells Black reporter
title_zh: 观看：特朗普告诉黑人记者，“显然，你永远不会注意到窗户被打破”
summary: President Donald Trump berated NBC News White House correspondent Yamiche Alcindor on Monday after she asked him to respond to critics who say he was too focused on construction projects in the nation's capital instead of issues with the country's airline syst
summary_zh: 周一，美国全国广播公司新闻 (NBC News) 白宫记者亚米切·阿尔辛多 (Yamiche Alcindor) 要求唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 总统对那些认为他
body_en: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-you-never-notice-broken-windows-obviously-trump-tells-black-reporter

President Donald Trump berated NBC News White House correspondent Yamiche Alcindor on Monday after she asked him to respond to critics who say he was too focused on construction projects in the nation's capital instead of issues with the country's airline systems, which came to a halt Friday in a rare nationwide FAA ground stop .
Watch Trump's remarks in the video player above.
After Trump called the White House "flawless," Alcindor attempted to follow up.
"Listen to me. I know you don't see dirt," Trump told Alcindor, who is Black.
The president went on to tell her, "You never notice broken windows, obviously, from where you come. I don't know. But we had 18 broken windows."
When Alcindor began to ask about taking responsibility, Trump called her "pathetic."

The episode is not the first time Trump has confronted Alcindor over her questions. When she was White House correspondent for the PBS News Hour in 2020, he criticized her for questions about his COVID-19 response, saying she asked a "nasty question."
